questions.prompt: What does this red octagonal traffic sign require you to do?
options: Come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line, and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic
Slow down to 5 mph and roll through if the intersection looks clear
Stop only if vehicles are approaching from your right
Yield without stopping unless a police officer is present
questions.explanation: In Texas, an octagonal red STOP sign means you must make a complete stop behind the stop line or crosswalk before entering the intersection.

questions.prompt: What does this downward-pointing red and white triangle sign mean?
options: Speed up to enter the highway ahead of oncoming traffic
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians on the road you are entering or crossing
Mandatory full stop for all vehicles at all times
Railroad tracks cross the highway ahead
questions.explanation: A YIELD sign requires you to slow down and give the right-of-way to cross traffic and pedestrians, stopping completely if necessary.

questions.prompt: What does this square white and red sign reading 'DO NOT ENTER' indicate?
options: HOV carpool lane entrance only
Road construction ahead; reduce speed to 25 mph
You are approaching a one-way roadway or exit ramp from the wrong direction; do not drive past this sign
No parking allowed along the curb
questions.explanation: The DO NOT ENTER sign marks the exit of a one-way road or ramp. Entering past this sign puts you head-on into opposing traffic.

questions.prompt: What does this sign with a red circle and diagonal slash over a left arrow tell drivers?
options: Sharp curve to the left ahead
Left lane ends ahead; merge right
Left turn permitted on green arrow only
Left turns are prohibited at this intersection
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a black left-turn arrow means left turns are illegal at that location.

questions.prompt: What does this regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow mean?
options: U-turns are prohibited at this location
Hairpin curve ahead; slow to 15 mph
Turnaround lane for buses only
Divided highway ends ahead
questions.explanation: This No U-Turn sign prohibits turning your vehicle around to travel in the opposite direction.

questions.prompt: What does this yellow diamond sign showing a car with wavy skid marks warn you about?
options: Winding road with sharp S-curves ahead
The road ahead is slippery when wet; reduce speed and avoid sudden braking or sharp turns
Gravel shoulder drop-off ahead
High-wind area ahead
questions.explanation: The Slippery When Wet warning sign alerts drivers to slow down when the pavement is wet or damp to prevent skidding or hydroplaning.

questions.prompt: What does this yellow diamond sign showing two arrows joining into one arrow indicate?
options: Divided highway begins ahead
Two-way traffic ahead
Merging traffic ahead; be prepared for vehicles entering your lane
Center turn lane begins ahead
questions.explanation: This Merge sign warns you that traffic from another roadway or ramp is merging into your lane ahead.

questions.prompt: What does this circular yellow sign with a black 'X' and 'RR' warn drivers about?
options: Road closed ahead for bridge inspection
A rest area and picnic site are ahead
An intersection of two farm-to-market roads is ahead
You are approaching a railroad crossing; look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR gives advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.prompt: What does this five-sided (pentagon) sign with two walking figures mean?
options: You are entering a school zone or approaching a school crossing
Pedestrians are prohibited on this highway
Public transit bus stop ahead
State park hiking trail entrance
questions.explanation: A five-sided pentagon sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crosswalk ahead. Slow down and watch carefully for children.

questions.prompt: What does a rectangular white sign reading 'SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT' require you to do on a multi-lane Texas highway?
options: Use the unpaved right shoulder whenever a faster car approaches
Drive in the right lane if you are traveling slower than the normal flow of traffic, leaving the left lane for passing
Exit the highway at the next ramp if you drive under 70 mph
Stay in the far-left lane unless turning right
questions.explanation: On multi-lane highways, slower vehicles must stay in the right-hand lane so faster traffic can pass safely in the left lane.

questions.prompt: In Texas, when is it legal to make a left turn on a steady red traffic light?
options: At any intersection if no oncoming cars are visible
Whenever you are turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street
Only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street after coming to a complete stop, unless prohibited by a sign
Left turns on red are never legal under any circumstances in Texas
questions.explanation: Texas law permits a left turn on a steady red light ONLY when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping completely and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, provided no sign prohibits it.

questions.prompt: What does a green arrow displayed at the same time as a red traffic light indicate?
options: The lane is closed to passenger vehicles
You must stop and wait for the circular green light before turning
You may go straight or turn in any direction
You may proceed carefully in the direction of the green arrow after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians lawfully in the intersection
questions.explanation: A green arrow allows you to make a protected movement in the direction pointed by the arrow, even while the main signal shows red for other movements.

questions.prompt: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a two-way road indicate?
options: Passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions
Passing is allowed during daylight hours only
Traffic in both lanes is traveling in the same direction
Passing is allowed if the vehicle ahead is traveling 5 mph below the limit
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow center lines prohibit vehicles in either direction from crossing the center line to pass another vehicle.

questions.prompt: What does a solid white line between lanes of traffic moving in the same direction mean?
options: Opposing traffic is traveling in the adjacent lane
You should stay in your lane and not cross the solid white line unless avoiding a hazard
Passing is encouraged across the line
The lane is for two-way left turns
questions.explanation: A solid white line between lanes of same-direction traffic discourages or prohibits lane changes near intersections, curves, or hazards.

questions.prompt: When approaching a railroad crossing where red lights are flashing or a gate is lowered, where must you stop in Texas?
options: At least 200 feet back from the crossing
Within 5 feet of the nearest rail
Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed
You may drive around the lowered gate if you do not see a train
questions.explanation: Texas law requires you to stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest railroad track when flashing red lights, bells, gates, or a flagger warn of an approaching train. Never drive around lowered gates.

questions.prompt: At an uncontrolled intersection of two streets of equal size, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who must yield?
options: The pickup truck always has the right-of-way over a sedan
The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left
The slower vehicle must always go first
The driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right
questions.explanation: When two vehicles enter an uncontrolled intersection at the same time from different roads, the driver on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.prompt: When a single or two-lane road intersects with a multi-lane divided highway (three or more lanes) without traffic signals, who must yield?
options: The driver on the smaller one- or two-lane road must yield to traffic on the multi-lane divided highway
Traffic on the multi-lane divided highway must stop for side-street cars
Whoever flashes their headlights first has the right-of-way
Only commercial trucks must yield
questions.explanation: In Texas, a driver on a single- or two-lane unpaved or secondary road intersecting a paved multi-lane highway must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the larger road.

questions.prompt: When entering a street from a private road, alley, or driveway in Texas, you must:
options: Accelerate quickly into the nearest lane before signaling
Stop prior to the sidewalk and yield the right-of-way to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians
Honk your horn so pedestrians step back onto the curb
Yield only to vehicles approaching from the left
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, private road, or driveway, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk and yield to all pedestrians and approaching vehicles.

questions.prompt: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield the right-of-way to:
options: Vehicles waiting behind you in the left-turn lane
Only vehicles turning left from the opposite direction
Any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction that is in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard, plus pedestrians
No one if the traffic light is solid green
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left on a solid green light must yield to all oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

questions.prompt: When an emergency vehicle (police car, fire engine, or ambulance) approaches with sirens and flashing lights active, you must:
options: Speed up to stay ahead of the ambulance
Stop immediately in the left passing lane
Follow closely behind the emergency vehicle to get through traffic faster
Yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right edge of the roadway clear of any intersection and stopping until it has passed
questions.explanation: Pull immediately to the right edge of the road (never block an intersection) and come to a full stop until the emergency vehicle passes. Also stay at least 500 feet behind any responding fire truck.

questions.prompt: When driving on a freeway frontage/feeder road in Texas, who has the right-of-way when a vehicle is exiting the freeway onto the frontage road?
options: Vehicles exiting the freeway via the exit ramp have the right-of-way; frontage road traffic must yield
Frontage road traffic always has the right-of-way over freeway exit ramps
Whichever vehicle is in the left lane of the frontage road
Only commercial trucks have the right-of-way
questions.explanation: In Texas, drivers traveling on a freeway frontage road must yield the right-of-way to vehicles leaving the freeway on an exit ramp (often marked with 'YIELD TO RAMP' signs).

questions.prompt: In Texas, you must activate your turn signal continuously for at least how many feet before making a turn or changing lanes?
options: At least 25 feet before turning
At least 100 feet before turning
At least 500 feet in residential areas
Only after entering the intersection
questions.explanation: Texas law requires drivers to signal their intention to turn or change lanes continuously for at least the last 100 feet before turning.

questions.prompt: In Texas, passing on the left on a two-lane road is strictly prohibited within how many feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct, or tunnel?
options: Within 1,000 feet
Within 20 feet
Within 100 feet
Passing is always permitted at railroad crossings
questions.explanation: In Texas, it is illegal to drive on the left side of the road to pass within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing, or within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel when your view is obstructed.

questions.prompt: When making a right turn, how should you position and steer your vehicle?
options: Turn into the far-left lane of the cross street
Swing wide into the left lane before turning right
Turn from the center lane across the right lane
Signal at least 100 feet ahead, approach in the far-right lane close to the right curb, and turn into the right-hand lane of the cross street
questions.explanation: Both the approach for a right turn and the turn itself must be made as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway.

questions.prompt: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right in Texas?
options: Only when the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn, or on a multi-lane road with unobstructed pavement, WITHOUT driving off the paved roadway
Whenever you drive onto the unpaved dirt shoulder at highway speed
In a school zone when the car ahead is driving 20 mph
At an uncontrolled two-lane intersection
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right only when conditions permit doing so safely on the main-traveled pavement (never by driving off the paved road or shoulder to overtake in an unsafe manner).

questions.prompt: On a curve or grade (hill) on a two-lane highway, you may make a U-turn only if:
options: You honk your horn before turning
Your vehicle can be seen by drivers approaching from either direction within 500 feet
Your speed is under 30 mph
There is a solid double yellow line
questions.explanation: In Texas, you may not turn a vehicle to move in the opposite direction (U-turn) on a curve or approaching the crest of a grade unless your vehicle is visible to other drivers approaching from either direction within 500 feet.

questions.prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the default maximum speed limit on a street in an urban district (city/town) in Texas?
options: 20 mph
45 mph
30 mph
55 mph
questions.explanation: According to the Texas Driver Handbook, the default unposted speed limit in an urban district is 30 mph, and 15 mph in an alley.

questions.prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the default speed limit in an alley in Texas?
options: 10 mph
25 mph
30 mph
15 mph
questions.explanation: In Texas, the maximum speed limit in any alley is 15 mph unless otherwise posted.

questions.prompt: At 50 mph on dry pavement, approximately how many feet does an average passenger car require to perceive a hazard, react, and come to a complete stop?
options: About 229 feet (nearly the length of a city block)
About 40 feet
About 75 feet
About 15 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes both reaction distance and braking distance. At 50 mph, an average car travels about 55 feet during reaction time plus about 174 feet while braking, totaling roughly 229 feet.

questions.prompt: How does Texas's Basic Speed Law apply when driving in heavy rain, fog, or bumper-to-bumper traffic?
options: You are always safe and legal as long as you drive at the exact posted speed limit
You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions, even if that requires driving well below the posted speed limit
You must turn on your hazard flashers and maintain the posted speed limit
Speed limits only apply during daylight hours
questions.explanation: Texas law states that a driver may not drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the circumstances and hazards then existing.

questions.prompt: In good weather and normal traffic, what is the recommended minimum following distance behind another passenger vehicle?
options: Half a second
One car length at 65 mph
At least 2 to 3 seconds (and 4 seconds or more in poor weather or at highway speeds)
25 feet at all highway speeds
questions.explanation: Keeping at least a 2- to 3-second gap in city traffic and 4+ seconds at highway speeds or in bad weather gives you time to react and brake safely if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

source.title: Texas Driver Handbook
source.section: Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations - Following Distance

questions.prompt: In Texas, you may not park or stand a vehicle within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: 50 feet
5 feet
25 feet
15 feet
questions.explanation: Texas law prohibits parking or standing an unoccupied vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.prompt: In Texas, it is illegal to park a vehicle within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
options: 20 feet
5 feet
10 feet
100 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park or stand a vehicle within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, or within 30 feet of any flashing beacon, stop sign, or traffic control signal located at the side of a roadway.

questions.prompt: When parallel parking on a two-way street with a curb in Texas, your right-hand wheels must be within:
options: 36 inches of the curb
18 inches of the right-hand curb
4 feet of the curb
On top of the curb
questions.explanation: Texas law requires a parallel-parked vehicle to have its right-hand wheels within 18 inches of the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway.

questions.prompt: Before leaving a vehicle parked and unattended on a grade (hill), what steps must you take under Texas law?
options: Keep the front wheels straight ahead without setting the parking brake
Leave the engine idling in neutral with hazard lights on
Stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, set the parking brake effectively, and turn the front wheels to the curb or side of the highway
Turn the wheels toward the center of the road on a downhill slope
questions.explanation: Texas law requires drivers leaving a vehicle unattended to stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, set the parking brake, and—if on a grade—turn the front wheels to the curb or side.

questions.prompt: In Texas, who is required by law to wear a safety belt in a passenger vehicle?
options: Only when driving on interstate highways
Only the driver and front-seat passenger
Only passengers under 17 years of age
The driver and ALL passengers (both front and back seats)
questions.explanation: Texas law requires the driver and every passenger in a passenger vehicle—whether seated in the front or back seat—to be secured by a safety belt or child passenger safety seat.

source.title: Texas Driver Handbook
source.section: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive - Safety Belts

questions.prompt: Under Texas law, children younger than 8 years old must be secured in a child passenger safety seat system according to manufacturer instructions, UNLESS:
options: The child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches (57 inches)
The child weighs more than 35 pounds
The trip is shorter than 5 miles
The child is riding in the front seat
questions.explanation: In Texas, any child younger than 8 years old must ride in an appropriate child safety seat or booster seat unless the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches.

questions.prompt: What is the statewide law in Texas regarding reading, writing, or sending electronic text messages while driving?
options: Texting is legal on rural highways outside city limits
Texting while driving is illegal statewide for all drivers, and drivers under 18 are prohibited from using any wireless communication device while driving
Texting is legal whenever driving below 35 mph
Only commercial truck drivers are prohibited from texting
questions.explanation: Texas law prohibits all drivers from reading, writing, or sending electronic messages while operating a moving vehicle unless stopped. Additionally, drivers under 18 and learners with permits (first 6 months) may not use handheld or hands-free cell phones except in emergencies.

questions.prompt: Under Texas's Financial Responsibility Law (minimum auto liability insurance), what are the minimum coverage limits ('30/60/25') required for a passenger car?
options: $100,000 per person and $50,000 for property damage
$10,000 per person and $5,000 for property damage
$30,000 per injured person, up to $60,000 total per crash for injuries, and $25,000 for property damage
Liability insurance is optional if your car is paid off
questions.explanation: Texas requires minimum liability coverage of $30,000 for each injured person, at least $60,000 total per collision for bodily injuries, and at least $25,000 for property damage (30/60/25).

questions.prompt: In Texas, a driver aged 21 or older is legally intoxicated (DWI) when their Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) reaches or exceeds:
questions.explanation: Under Texas law, a person 21 or older is legally intoxicated if they have a Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or more, or if they lack the normal use of mental or physical faculties due to alcohol or drugs.

source.title: Texas Driver Handbook
source.section: Chapter 10: How Alcohol and Drugs Affect the Ability to Drive

questions.prompt: Under Texas's Zero Tolerance Law for minors (under age 21), what amount of detectable alcohol in the system makes it illegal to operate a motor vehicle in a public place?
options: Any detectable amount of alcohol (even below 0.08%) is an offense of Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol by a Minor (DUIA)
Only a BAC of 0.08% or higher
Only a BAC of 0.05% or higher
Minors may drive with a 0.04% BAC during daylight hours
questions.explanation: Texas has a strict Zero Tolerance law for drivers under 21: having ANY detectable amount of alcohol in a minor's system while driving is illegal.

questions.prompt: Under Texas's Implied Consent Law, if you are arrested for DWI and refuse to provide a breath or blood specimen, your driver license will be suspended for:
options: 15 days
At least 180 days on a first refusal
Only 24 hours
Your license cannot be suspended unless you admit guilt
questions.explanation: In Texas, refusing a chemical breath or blood test after a DWI arrest triggers an automatic Administrative License Revocation (ALR) suspension of 180 days for a first offense (and 2 years for repeat offenses).

questions.prompt: In Texas, possessing an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a motor vehicle located on a public highway is:
options: Legal if the container is kept in the unlocked glove box
Legal for passengers as long as the driver is not drinking
Illegal (a Class C misdemeanor), even if the vehicle is stopped or parked on the public roadway
Legal on rural county roads
questions.explanation: Texas Open Container Law makes it illegal to knowingly possess an open alcohol container in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a public highway (including the glove compartment). Open containers must be locked in the trunk or behind the last upright seat if there is no trunk.

questions.prompt: When must you turn on your vehicle's headlights in Texas?
options: Parking lights may be used instead of headlights at dusk
Only between 9:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
Only when visibility drops below 100 feet
From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, AND any time persons or vehicles cannot be seen clearly at 1,000 feet
questions.explanation: Texas law requires headlights to be turned on from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, and whenever visibility is less than 1,000 feet.

questions.prompt: When driving at night in Texas, you must dim your high-beam headlights to low beams within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle?
options: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle, and within 300 feet when following behind another vehicle
Within 100 feet of an oncoming vehicle
Within 1,500 feet in city traffic only
Only when the other driver flashes their high beams
questions.explanation: In Texas, drivers must switch from high beams to low beams within 500 feet of an approaching oncoming vehicle and within 300 feet when following behind another vehicle.

questions.prompt: When approaching a flooded roadway or low-water crossing during heavy rain in Texas ('Turn Around, Don't Drown'), how much moving water can sweep away most passenger cars and SUVs?
options: At least 6 feet of water is needed to move a car
As little as 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock down an adult, and 12 to 24 inches of water can float and sweep away most vehicles
Floodwater is safe to cross if you drive in low gear at 30 mph
Pickup trucks cannot be swept away by floodwater
questions.explanation: Never drive around barricades or into water covering a roadway. Six inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet, and 1 to 2 feet of water will float and carry away most cars, SUVs, and pickup trucks.

questions.prompt: Under the Texas 'Move Over / Slow Down' law, when approaching a stationary police car, emergency vehicle, tow truck, TxDOT vehicle, or utility vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside, you must:
options: Come to a full stop in the middle of the highway
Slow down by 5 mph and stay in the lane closest to the emergency vehicle
Vacate the lane closest to the stopped vehicle if on a multi-lane road, OR slow down to 20 mph below the posted speed limit (to 5 mph if the limit is 25 mph or less)
Honk your horn while passing at the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: Texas law requires you to either move out of the lane closest to the stopped emergency/tow/TxDOT vehicle OR reduce your speed to 20 mph below the posted speed limit (and to 5 mph on roads with a posted limit of 25 mph or less).

source.title: Texas Driver Handbook
source.section: Chapter 4: Move Over or Slow Down

questions.prompt: In Texas, when a school bus is stopped with alternating flashing red lights on a road divided ONLY by a left-turn lane (with no raised physical barrier or unpaved median), who must stop?
options: No one needs to stop if children are not visible
Only traffic directly behind the school bus must stop
Opposing traffic may pass at 25 mph because of the center left-turn lane
Drivers traveling in BOTH directions must stop and wait until the flashing red lights are turned off
questions.explanation: In Texas, a center two-way left-turn lane is NOT considered a physical median/barrier. Traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus flashing red lights unless the roadways are separated by an intervening unpaved space or physical barrier.

questions.prompt: When sharing the road with a motorcyclist in Texas, how much lane space is the motorcycle legally entitled to?
options: The full width of a traffic lane, just like a full-sized passenger car
Half of a lane so cars can share the same lane side-by-side
The paved shoulder only
The space between two lanes of traffic
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is entitled to the full width of a lane. Never attempt to share a lane side-by-side with a motorcyclist, and maintain extra following distance.

source.title: Texas Driver Handbook
source.section: Chapter 13: Sharing the Road with Motorcycles

questions.prompt: When passing a bicyclist on a road in Texas, what is the safest practice?
options: Pass within 12 inches while sounding your horn
Slow down, move into an adjacent lane if available, or leave a safe clearance of at least 3 feet for cars (6 feet for commercial trucks) when passing
Crowd the bicyclist onto the gravel shoulder
Follow closely behind the bicyclist with high beams on
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle operators on Texas roadways. Give them plenty of room (at least 3 feet for passenger cars) and change lanes when possible to pass safely.

lessons.title: Texas Traffic Signs: Shapes, Colors & Meanings
lessons.body:
• Octagon (Red): STOP completely before the crosswalk or stop line.
• Downward Triangle (Red/White): YIELD right-of-way.
• Vertical White Rectangle: Regulatory laws (Speed Limit, Slower Traffic Keep Right, Do Not Pass).
• Yellow Diamond: Warning of road hazards ahead.
• Orange Diamond: Road construction and maintenance work zones (fines double in Texas work zones when workers are present).
• Round Yellow with X & RR: Railroad crossing ahead.

lessons.title: Texas Traffic Signals, Railroad Crossings & Markings
lessons.body:
• Red Light Turns: Right turn on red is allowed after a full stop unless prohibited by sign. Left turn on red is allowed ONLY from a one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping.
• Railroad Crossings: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail when red lights flash or gates lower.
• Double Solid Yellow Lines: No passing from either direction.
• Broken Yellow Line: Passing allowed on the side with the broken line when clear.

lessons.title: Texas Right-of-Way Rules & Frontage Roads
lessons.body:
• Uncontrolled Intersections: Yield to the vehicle on your RIGHT.
• T-Intersections & Secondary Roads: Yield to traffic on the continuing through street or multi-lane divided highway.
• Freeway Exit Ramps & Frontage Roads: Traffic on a frontage/feeder road must yield to vehicles exiting the freeway.
• Emergency Vehicles: Pull to the right edge and stop; stay at least 500 feet behind responding fire apparatus.

lessons.title: Signaling, No-Passing Zones & U-Turns in Texas
lessons.body:
• Turn Signals: Signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes.
• No-Passing Zones: Never pass on the left within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.
• U-Turns on Curves/Hills: Legal only if your vehicle can be seen for at least 500 feet in both directions.

lessons.title: Texas Speed Limits & Stopping Distance
lessons.body:
• 30 mph: Default unposted speed limit in an urban district (city/town street).
• 15 mph: Default unposted speed limit in an alley.
• 70 mph: Default daytime speed limit on rural state/US numbered highways outside urban districts (unless posted higher or lower).
• Stopping Distance: At 50 mph, average stopping distance is ~229 feet; at 70 mph, ~387 feet.

lessons.title: Texas Parking Distances & Parallel Parking
lessons.body:
• Parallel Parking: Right wheels must be within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.
• Prohibited Distances:
  - Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
  - Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
  - Within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic control signal.
  - Within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

lessons.title: Seat Belts, Child Seats, Texting & 30/60/25 Insurance
lessons.body:
• Seat Belts: Mandatory for driver and ALL passengers (front and back seats).
• Child Safety Seats: Required for children under age 8 unless taller than 4 feet 9 inches.
• Texting Ban: Reading, writing, or sending texts while driving is illegal statewide; drivers under 18 may not use any wireless device while driving.
• Liability Insurance (30/60/25): Minimum $30,000 per injured person, $60,000 per crash, and $25,000 property damage.

lessons.title: Texas DWI, Minor Zero Tolerance & Implied Consent
lessons.body:
• 0.08% BAC: Legal intoxication limit (DWI) for drivers 21 and older.
• Zero Tolerance (Under 21): ANY detectable amount of alcohol is illegal (DUIA by a Minor).
• Implied Consent: Refusing a breath/blood test after a DWI arrest results in an automatic 180-day license suspension on a first offense.
• Open Container Law: Open alcohol containers are prohibited in the passenger area of any motor vehicle on a public highway.

lessons.title: Headlights, High-Beam Dimming & Flood Safety
lessons.body:
• Headlights Required: 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever visibility is under 1,000 feet.
• Dimming High Beams: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 300 feet when following another vehicle.
• Flooded Roads: 'Turn Around, Don't Drown'—1 to 2 feet of water can sweep away most cars and trucks.

lessons.title: Texas Move Over / Slow Down (20 mph) & School Buses
lessons.body:
• Move Over / Slow Down Law: Vacate the lane closest to a stopped emergency, tow, TxDOT, or utility vehicle with flashing lights, OR slow down to 20 mph below the posted limit (5 mph if the limit is 25 mph or less).
• School Buses: Stop from both directions unless the highway is separated by a raised physical barrier or unpaved median space (a center left-turn lane is NOT a barrier).
